rationale: Parkinson self-reports after broccoli tea containing ground untreated mustard include little tremor improvement and occasional transient worsening. A dietary menu lists unspecified mustard and gives no rest-tremor result. A mustard-derived enzyme preparation is a pending constituent lead without separately measured rest tremor. Toasted seed remains unresolved.

A Parkinson case describes mood change during combined daikenchuto and rehabilitation. Extract studies in mice show behavioral changes, with one report internally inconsistent. A controlled Nepalese pepper extract trial in healthy adults did not give a clear mood contrast at individual tests and did not measure depression. The toasted spice direction remains unresolved.

People report using coconut oil among several strategies for coping with OFF periods. A separate qualitative high-fat meal account has no oil identification. The randomized medium-chain triglyceride comparison used an ordinal OFF result that differed before treatment. These do not give a refined coconut oil estimate for daily OFF time.

A randomized plant-rich Parkinson diet study observed no clear change in Epworth daytime sleepiness and gives no raw-carrot exposure. General-population blood carotenoid associations vary in direction, with no raw-carrot-specific result.

Some allergic children had hoarseness during ground roasted hazelnut challenges. Edible oil intake, vocal loudness, and Parkinson hypophonia were not established. A separate pooled pediatric report also uses a different voice and throat outcome.

One case reports dysarthria after concentrated clove oil and did not establish causation. The clove gargle and Parkinson mixed-odor exposures did not report individual intelligibility. The evidence leaves ground clove and listener-rated Parkinson speech unresolved.

A Parkinson screening study used dill pickle odor. A post-COVID protocol registered an olfactory training set with dill among eleven odors and no results. These are odor exposures without a fresh-dill ingestion comparison in Parkinson disease.

A cumin essential-oil case series reported unquantified dizziness without a posture or control. The ground cumin and essential-oil trials measured resting blood pressure, and the Parkinson diet survey supplied no ingredient-specific standing symptom. Direction remains unresolved.

A pediatric ADHD trial reports lower inattention scores after almond syrup, with a baseline imbalance and no clearly reported adjusted comparison for the endpoint. An Alzheimer powdered-almond trial was inconclusive. Differences in formulation and population leave cold-pressed oil and Parkinson attention unresolved.

Insomnia severity improved in both arms of a CBD pilot that used corn oil in both groups. The trial had no oil-free arm. Other trials compare fish oil or a drug to corn oil. One planned PSQI result is unreported and another sleep publication was retracted. No trial establishes an effect of refined corn oil on Parkinson insomnia.

A Parkinson whole-diet comparison used boiled potato in mixed meals and did not isolate its effect on sleepiness. A pediatric mash crossover registered acute sleepiness and the probable linked abstract omits that outcome. Frying and baking protocols measure related symptoms with no boiled-potato result.
